# ScatterChart

Scatter chart: the relation between two values, one point per item. Points are 8 px dots with a 2 px ring in
the surface color, so overlapping points stay readable.

**Interaction**: the pointer does not have to land on a dot: the nearest point within 16 px shows its tooltip
and lifts. `Tab` focuses the chart (focus ring only for the keyboard); `←` / `→` move between points in order of
their horizontal value with the same tooltip, `Home` / `End` jump to the first and last, `Esc` hides the
tooltip. Legend items show and hide series without changing colors; the table view lists every point.

**Category**: Charts · **Common uses**: Correlation between two measures (price and sales, size and duration), spotting outliers

## Import

```ts
import { ScatterChart } from 'vellum-ui'
```

## Basic usage

One point per item; `xLabel` and `yLabel` name the axes. The pointer only has to be near a dot: the nearest
point within 16 px shows its tooltip.

```tsx
export function Basic() {
  return (
    <ScatterChart
      title="Price and units sold"
      description="Last quarter, per product"
      xLabel="Price"
      yLabel="Units sold"
      xFormat={(v) => `$${v}`}
      series={[{ key: 'products', name: 'Products', points: products }]}
    />
  )
}
```

## Variants

### Two series

Up to 3 series: in a scatter chart any two points can be neighbors, and only the first 3 chart colors are told
apart in every pair. For more groups, fold them into "Other" or use small multiples.

```tsx
export function Series() {
  return (
    <ScatterChart
      title="Build size and duration"
      xLabel="Size (MB)"
      yLabel="Duration (s)"
      series={[
        { key: 'main', name: 'Main branch', points: builds(0, 3) },
        { key: 'feature', name: 'Feature branches', points: builds(30, 5) },
      ]}
    />
  )
}
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default | Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `series` | `readonly ScatterSeries[]` | The series and their points. Use at most 3 series: in a scatter chart any two points can be neighbors, and only the first 3 chart colors are told apart in every pair. | — | Yes |
| `xFormat` | `ValueFormat` | How horizontal values are written on the axis, in the tooltip and in the table. | `'auto'` | No |
| `yFormat` | `ValueFormat` | How vertical values are written on the axis, in the tooltip and in the table. | `'auto'` | No |
| `xLabel` | `string` | Name of the horizontal axis: shown under the axis, in the tooltip and as a table header. | — | No |
| `yLabel` | `string` | Name of the vertical axis: shown along the axis, in the tooltip and as a table header. | — | No |
| `emphasis` | `string` | Key of the one series the chart is about: it keeps its color and the others use the muted color. | — | No |
| `title` | `string` | Title of the chart: what is plotted. It is also the accessible name of the graphic. | — | No |
| `description` | `string` | A short description under the title, such as the period or the unit. | — | No |
| `height` | `number` | Height of the graphic in pixels, axis labels included. The states take the same height. The table view starts at this height and grows with its rows up to 480 px (or this height when it is taller); only longer tables scroll. | `240` | No |
| `loading` | `boolean` | Loading: without data, a delayed loading indicator takes the place of the graphic; with data, the previous graphic stays at reduced opacity until the new data arrives. | — | No |
| `error` | `ReactNode` | Error: `true` shows the default error state; a node is shown as the message of the error state. | — | No |
| `onRetry` | `() => void` | Retry after an error; shows a "Retry" button in the error state. | — | No |
| `emptyDescription` | `ReactNode` | Text of the empty state when there is no data, "No data" by default (follows `locale`). | — | No |
| `actions` | `ReactNode` | Actions in the top-right corner, before the view switch (for example a menu or a time range). | — | No |
| `plain` | `boolean` | Without the card (no background, shadow or padding), for charts inside a Panel, a dialog or a drawer. | — | No |

Also accepts `testId` (rendered as `data-testid`), `aria-label`, `role` and `id`, like all primitives.

Does not accept `style` or `className`: appearance is adjusted only through the semantic props above and the theme.
